Divine: the Lord (2Ki 3:14, 2Ch 6:19, Psa 28:5, 144:3, Isa 5:12, Jer 24:5, Lam 4:16), God (2Ch 6:19, Job 35:13, Psa 80:14, Ecc 3:18, Jer 24:5, 1Cor 4:1, 1Ti 6:1, 1Pe 5:12) and Christ (1Cor 4:1, 2Cor 5:16). Human: Cain (Gen 4:5), the men set to labour (Exo 5:9, Job 37:24), the patriarchs and the servants (Deu 9:27, 2Ch 6:19), Samson (Jdg 15:3), Nabal and the young men (1Sa 25:25), Elisha and Jehoshaphat (2Ki 3:14), the priests (2Ch 5:11, Lam 4:16), man (Psa 144:3, Ecc 3:18, Isa 33:8, 1Cor 4:1) and a brother (2Th 3:15, 1Pe 5:12). The potter appears in Isa 29:16 and Lam 4:2 as the figure of the one who makes. In the verses of the Lord's regard the one regarded is a person or a people; in the verses of persons, one regards another. This record does not compare the group with the others.

fill.obs_text: The direction of the regard is stated in four ways. God regards persons or refuses to: the Lord's regard for the exiles (Jer 24:5), for the vine (Psa 80:14), for the covenant (Psa 74:20), his lack of regard for Cain's offering (Gen 4:5), for the empty cry (Job 35:13) and for the wise in conceit (Job 37:24), his not looking on the priests (Lam 4:16). Persons ask God for regard: Moses (Deu 9:27), Solomon (2Ch 6:19), the psalmist (Psa 119:117), Hannah (1Sa 1:16). Persons regard or fail to regard one another: Elisha for Jehoshaphat (2Ki 3:14), the Medes for silver (Isa 13:17), the master and the servant (1Ti 6:1), the brother (2Th 3:15). And persons are regarded by others as something else: the daughters as foreigners (Gen 31:15), the faithful as sheep (Psa 44:22, Rom 8:36), the disciples among themselves (Luk 22:24). The direction changes: from God to persons, from persons to God, between persons, and of persons by others.

fill.obs_text: The surface regard carries many codes in this group, and the verses show several senses. It names a look of attention: H8159 (Gen 4:5, Psa 119:117), H5027 (Psa 74:20, Isa 5:12, Lam 4:16), H7200G (Deu 33:9, Job 37:24), H7789 (Job 35:13), H6485I (Psa 80:14), H6437G (Deu 9:27, 2Ch 6:19). It names an understanding or knowing: H0995 in Psa 28:5, H3045 in Job 9:21, Psa 144:3 and Pro 12:10, G1097 and G6063 in 2Cor 5:16, H7919A in Job 34:27, H5234A (to recognise) in Jer 24:5. It names a reckoning: H2803H in Isa 13:17 and 33:8, G3049 in 1Cor 4:1 and 1Pe 5:12, H6188 in Lev 19:23. It names a taking up of favour: H5375Q in 2Ki 3:14, H5414I in 1Sa 1:16. And in some verses the translated regard is a ground or a small word: H1700 (a matter) in Ecc 3:18, G3313 (a part) in Col 2:16, G4012 (about) in Act 28:22, H8104J (to keep) in 2Ch 5:11, and H0853, H9006 and H3820A in the units of Jdg 15:3 and 1Sa 25:25. So the surface is a word for attention by look, by knowing, by reckoning and by favour, with some verses where it is not regard at all.

fill.obs_text: The surface regarded carries four codes in this group. H2803H stands in Gen 31:15, Psa 44:22, Lam 4:2 and Hos 8:12 for the account made of persons or things by another, usually a lowering; H2803J stands in Isa 29:16 and 29:17 for the equating of one thing with another; G1380 stands in Luk 22:24 for the disciples' reckoning of rank; G3049 stands in Rom 2:26 and 8:36 for the account made by God or by others. The first two are the Hebrew of one root (to think, account), and the Greek verbs differ: G1380 is to seem or be thought, G3049 to count or credit. The sense in all is an account made of someone or something, passive in every verse.
